## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 69 (*Pavattinī-nānubandhana*, "Not following a mentor") is a monastic disciplinary rule for Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunī*s) in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a nun who fails to attend to and follow her preceptor (*pavattinī*) for a period of two years commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Within the Pali tradition, the rule is paralleled in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pācittiya 69) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pācittiya 69) [SuttaCentral]. Full parallels in other Vinaya lineages are preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit texts, including the Dharmaguptaka Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Pācittiya 129), Sarvāstivāda Pātimokkha and Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 113 and 115), Mahāsāṅghika Pātimokkha and Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 105), and the Sanskrit Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 105) [SuttaCentral].
